conventions.convention: Signature is (−,+,+,+); O is nonempty, connected and open; ξ is smooth, future timelike and Killing; N=√(−g(ξ,ξ)) and u=ξ/N. Length coordinates use x⁰=ct, with dimensionless metric components and lapse. The inherited foundational assumption is AC_ω.
A is a global smooth real one-form; F_ab=∂_a A_b−∂_b A_a and (ι_ξ F)_a=ξᵇF_ba. A global compensator, when assumed, satisfies L_ξ A=dΛ_ξ. Set Ψ_ξ=ξᵃA_a−Λ_ξ and Φ_ξ=−cΨ_ξ.

m>0, M=mc², P=Mw and g(w,w)=−1. Trajectories are C² curves on open real intervals, parametrized by s_m=cτ, satisfying ∇_w Pᵃ=cqFᵃ_b wᵇ. Charged transport has horizontal velocity P and covariant vertical acceleration cqFᵃ_b Pᵇ.

Stationarity means L_F,q f=0 on the entire future massive shell, with f=exp(ζ+g(β,P)), β=u/(k_B T), T>0 and ζ=μ/(k_B T). The first equivalence needs no global compensator; the global redshift equivalence additionally requires one. Charge q may be zero.
Gauge changes are A↦A+dχ and Λ_ξ↦Λ_ξ+ξ(χ), leaving H_ξ invariant. A potential-reference shift Φ_ξ↦Φ_ξ+C₀ changes H_ξ by qC₀.

The finite entropy theorem uses r≥1, open convex cell domains, C¹ concave entropies, continuous particle-number coordinates, N_i>0 and positive energy derivatives at a supplied feasible interior point. Stationarity tests every variation in ker A; no existence or boundary attainment is claimed.
S¹_L=R/LZ with L>0; the global closed one-form ϑ has positive circle period L. The obstruction assumes qE₀≠0 and constant T_K>0, and concerns single-valued global smooth scalars.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the smooth stationary Lorentzian data, global potential A, F=dA, optional potential-symmetry compensator, force and contraction signs, future massive shell, charged transport field, exponential ansatz and gauge transformations.

For the stated smooth stationary data with m>0, T>0, β=u/(k_B T), ζ=μ/(k_B T) and f=exp(ζ+g(β,P)), whole-future-mass-shell stationarity is equivalent to β being Killing and dζ=−cqι_β F. With a global smooth compensator, these conditions are equivalent to constants T_K>0 and μ_K satisfying NT=T_K, β=ξ/(k_B T_K) and Nμ+qΦ_ξ=μ_K; the local and compensated-energy exponents agree.

For the smooth data of def-tgr-charged-liouville-data with m>0, the future massive shell is a smooth hypersurface of TO and the charged transport vector field is tangent to it, giving a well-defined smooth restriction.

Under the stated global potential symmetry, ι_ξ F=−dΨ_ξ and H_ξ=−g(P,ξ)+qΦ_ξ is constant along every stated charged trajectory. It is invariant under the paired gauge transformation; shifting Φ_ξ by C₀ shifts H_ξ by qC₀.

Under the stated finite-cell, interior-point and positive-energy-derivative hypotheses, stationarity under every independent exchange variation is equivalent to constants T_K>0 and μ_K with N_iT_i=T_K and N_iμ_i+qΦ_i=μ_K. Concavity gives a global feasible maximum; strict concavity gives uniqueness whenever it exists.
